skill.name: tdd-workflows-tdd-cycle
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants through a strict test-driven development workflow with fail-first tests, minimal implementation, refactoring, coverage checks, and review gates.
skill.summary: Run a structured red-green-refactor cycle with checkpoints for tests, coverage, refactoring, and final review.
skill.author: sickn33

The text is failure recovery guidance to return to a valid development state. It does not request host inspection, system enumeration, or data collection.

The heading asks the assistant to verify test success. It does not describe network scanning, network discovery, or external communication.
The checklist item says all tests should pass. This is normal testing language and provides no network reconnaissance instruction.
The line warns against writing tests that already pass. It is a TDD quality warning, not a network behavior or discovery step.
The line warns against modifying tests to force success. It contains no network access, scanning, or external target discovery.

content.value_statement: Teams often skip fail-first testing and lose design feedback. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a strict red-green-refactor workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines acceptance criteria, edge cases, and test scenarios before implementation begins.
Guides failing unit tests, failure verification, minimal implementation, and refactoring.
Adds integration, performance, and edge-case tests after core behavior works.
Sets coverage thresholds and refactoring triggers for quality checkpoints.
Supports incremental test-by-test work and full suite mode.
Tracks TDD cycle metrics, coverage progression, and review outcomes.
limitations: Does not provide executable scripts or project-specific test commands.
References subagent types that may not exist in every AI environment.
Coverage thresholds may need adjustment for each repository.
Cannot guarantee test quality without human review and clear requirements.

use_cases.title: Ship Features Test First
use_cases.description: Use the red-green-refactor loop to build new behavior from clear acceptance criteria and failing tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Automation
use_cases.description: Create repeatable unit, integration, performance, and edge-case testing steps for a development team.

use_cases.title: Review TDD Compliance
use_cases.description: Check whether a feature followed fail-first testing, coverage checkpoints, and refactoring expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this TDD cycle to <feature>. Start by defining acceptance criteria, edge cases, and failing unit tests. Do not implement production code yet.

prompt_templates.title: Use Incremental Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Use incremental mode for <feature>. Write one failing test, implement only enough code, then refactor before the next test.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use suite mode for <module>. Design the full failing test suite, implement the smallest passing solution, then add integration tests.

prompt_templates.title: Audit TDD Discipline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review <feature> against this TDD workflow. Identify any broken phase, missing checkpoint, coverage gap, or refactoring issue.

output_examples.input: Create a payment validation feature using TDD.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists acceptance criteria, writes failing unit tests, verifies the failures, implements only required logic, then refactors with tests passing.

output_examples.input: Use incremental TDD for a search filter.
output_examples.output: The assistant handles one behavior at a time, keeps each implementation minimal, and records coverage progress after each cycle.

output_examples.input: Review whether this feature followed TDD.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports phase violations, missing tests, coverage gaps, and refactoring needs, then recommends concrete recovery steps.

best_practices: Confirm each test fails for the expected reason before writing implementation.
Keep green-phase code limited to the behavior required by failing tests.
Run the relevant test suite after every refactoring step.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation code before a failing test exists.
Changing tests only to make broken production code pass.
Skipping refactoring after tests become green.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the AI assistant to run project test commands when available.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for AI coding assistants and supports those tools.

faq.question: Does it require a specific programming language?
faq.answer: No. It describes a TDD process that can apply across languages and test frameworks.

faq.question: What does incremental mode mean?
faq.answer: Incremental mode focuses on one failing test, one minimal implementation, and one refactor at a time.

faq.question: What does suite mode mean?
faq.answer: Suite mode writes a broader failing test set before implementing the full feature behavior.

faq.question: Can the coverage thresholds be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. The listed thresholds are defaults and should match repository standards when needed.
